content.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` ## few_shots.md Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## review_verdict_rules.md # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, doc-comment refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, doc-comment refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from a release bump or pin PR strands that PR behind the standard queue. - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges. ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:

Closes #2004

Removed the on-device Gemma stack end-to-end: `flutter_gemma` + `flutter_gemma_litertlm` packages and their pinned web transitive deps, `lib/gemma/` (9 files), gema wiring in `agent_service*`/`last_connection`/`quota_store`/`analytics`/`boot`, settings/model-cache/quick-start UI and l10n strings (en/ru), pod plumbing (iOS/macOS), web helpers (`inline_script_6.js`, `cache_api.js`, `opfs_helper.js`), and the CI seed/dylib steps (`.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed`, macOS companion-dylib seeding, iOS `LiteRtLm` keep-set grep). Net: 117 files, −6.5k/+0.8k lines.

### Key decisions

- **No migration, silent reset** — persisted `boot`/`last_connection`/on-device stores carrying a `gemma` kind reset to the default cloud connection on load (`last_connection.dart`, `ondevice_config_store.dart` keep tolerant old-bytes parse; `markConfigured('gemma')` now refuses).

- **`lib/on_device/` stays** — the ticket listed it for deletion, but it is now the shared pump/codec skeleton of the surviving WebLLM + transformers.js engines (verified: both stream functions import it).
- **AC1 raw grep residue is intentional** — the non-goal stacks (`transformers_js`, `webllm` catalogs), the removal machinery, and the two reset codecs are the only remaining token hits; `test/gemma_removal_gate_test.dart` (AC7 REG) encodes exactly this allowlist and makes any other `gemma|litert|litertlm|mediapipe` hit under `flutter_app/lib` or `pubspec.yaml` red.

Baselines were restored byte-for-byte; the 3 gema-affected goldens (`sections_cache_settings`, `setup_quick_start_desktop/phone`) need the documented `flutter test test/golden --update-goldens` re-bake on the release runner. `sections_quick_start.png` was deleted with its widget (orphan gate green).
- iOS 16 floor kept (per ticket: no blind revert; follow-up card evaluates lowering).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #2006._

> ℹ️ **5 resolved thread(s) excluded; 10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-30):

🚨 **BLOCKING: first-boot cleanup can recursively delete USER project content (data loss), and misses the real cache exactly there**

`cleanupGemmaLeftovers` walks `env.cwd` and deletes, silently and recursively:

```dart
var root = env.cwd;                      // line 110
...
if (info.kind == FileKind.directory) {
  if (name.contains(_storageDirFragment)) {          // ANY dir whose NAME contains "flutter_gemma"
    final result = await env.remove(path, recursive: true);
```

The docstring assumption — *"the sandbox cwd (the app-documents root the plugin stored under)"* — does not hold on desktop with a **mounted project folder**. Boot chain: `FaAppBoot.run()` → `createPlatformEnv()` → `createDesktopEnv()` → `mountedDesktopEnv()` → `ProjectMountEnv` with `cwd == '/project'` (flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart, flutter_app/lib/services/project_mount_env.dart). `ProjectMountEnv.listDir`/`remove` map `/project/...` onto the **user-selected host folder**, so on every boot this walk:

1. **Recursively deletes any directory in the user's real project whose name contains `flutter_gemma`** — e.g. a vendored `third_party/flutter_gemma/` checkout, a `docs/flutter_gemma_notes/` folder, test fixtures — plus any `*.litertlm` file it finds. Silent, no confirmation, runs every boot (not just first).
2. **Misses the actual plugin cache in that same configuration** — the app-container root (`_delegate.cwd`) is never walked when a mount is active, so the stated goal fails exactly where user data is put at risk.

This is unbounded destruction of non-app-owned content: the flutter_gemma plugin never stored anything in the *user's project folder*; `docs/flutter_gemma_notes/` is as much a false positive as `keep-me.txt` is in the unit test. `leftover_model_cleanup_test.dart` only covers a flat in-memory sandbox, so the mount case is untested.

Suggested fix (pick one or more):
- Resolve the walk root to the **app-owned container** (unwrap `ProjectMountEnv`/decorators the way `SessionCwd.sessionCwd` does) instead of `env.cwd`, and explicitly skip the `projectMountSegment` (`/project`);
- anchor directory deletion to the plugin's exact storage names (e.g. `flutter_gemma` as an exact/known-layout dir, not a `contains` fragment) and restrict the walk to directories the plugin owned;
- add a test with a `ProjectMountEnv`-style env proving user files under the mounted root survive a boot.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-30):

🚨 **BLOCKING: 3 golden baselines are stale — the nightly macOS golden leg will fail right after merge**

The scenarios that render these frames changed, but the committed PNGs did not:

- `setup_quick_start_desktop.png` / `setup_quick_start_phone.png` — the scripted engines lost the `GemmaInstalledModel('gemma-4-E4B-it.litertlm', 4.3 GB)` row and the widget no longer renders gema rows, so the rendered frame differs from the baseline (the `sections_quick_start.png` sibling was correctly **deleted** with its test).
- `sections_cache_settings.png` (sections_golden_test.dart:294) — the stacked cache sections no longer include `GemmaCacheSection` (+24px spacing gone), baseline unchanged.

`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- flutter_app/test/golden/goldens/` touches only the deleted `sections_quick_start.png` — confirming the three baselines were restored byte-for-byte. `flutter test/golden` runs on the nightly macOS row with the pinned 3.47.4 SDK (nightly.yml), and its red feeds the deduped nightly-red issue — i.e. this merge knowingly breaks a documented guard.

The PR's own project memory (memory/note/n_1018_80a7.md, committed here) says baselines must be re-baked on the pinned macOS release runner and that local re-bakes corrupt them — so the fix is process, not pixels:

1. land the documented `flutter test test/golden --update-goldens` re-bake on the release runner for `sections_cache_settings`, `setup_quick_start_desktop`, `setup_quick_start_phone` **before or with the merge**, or
2. get explicit owner sign-off on a follow-up card that owns the red nightly window, linked from this PR, so the re-bake is guaranteed to land.

Also see the sibling thread: the golden **coverage guard** (not just the pixel diffs) is red on this head because `downloaded_models_quick_start.dart` lost its map entry.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-30):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: dead public wrapper + misplaced alias comment — in a PR whose goal is "zero dead code"**

/// gh-2004 boot hook: neutral-named alias so call sites (app_boot) do not

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-30):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "removed kinds" fact is now encoded twice — hoist one shared constant**

gh-2004's removed-kind knowledge lives in two independent private encodings:

- `last_connection.dart:175` — `bool _isRemovedKind(String providerKind) => providerKind == 'gemma';`

💡 **SUGGESTION: web cleanup covers OPFS only — confirm no CacheStorage / registry leftovers survive**

The doc claim is "web: the OPFS root, deleting the same shapes". That matches the **streaming** path the app actually used (`gemma_service_plugin.dart` initialized `WebStorageMode.streaming` — weights streamed into the OPFS root as `*.litertlm`, which `listRoot()`/`removeEntry` handle). # Note: n_1018_80a7

flutter_app golden baselines (test/golden/goldens/*.png) are captured only on the pinned macOS release runner with Flutter 3.47.4 (nightly pins it; ci.yml ubuntu shards exclude goldens). A linux dev host CANNOT reproduce them — even untouched baselines like setup_first_run_phone.png fail pixel-diff locally on the pinned SDK clone. After UI changes: restore/delete PNGs to match the widget surface, run `python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (orphan/existence gate), and leave the actual `flutter test test/golden --update-goldens` re-bake to the release flow; committing locally rendered PNGs breaks the macOS leg. Also: the agent's own session exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE, which makes flutter_app test/providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart fail with 'FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env wins' — run with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` to verify.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: on mobile the walk root may not contain the plugin's storage — the cleanup could no-op exactly where it matters (please confirm the plugin's IO layout)**

The mount fix is correct, but it pinned the walk root to `env.cwd`, and on Android/iOS that is the app sandbox, not the app documents root where a Flutter plugin stores by default:

- `env_factory_io.dart:76-77`: the mobile sandbox is `<appDir>/fah_sandbox` (`getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox`) and the boot env's cwd is the **sandbox**, not `appDir`;
- the removed stack was initialized with default storage — base `gemma_service_plugin.dart:88-91` passed only `inferenceEngines` + `webStorageMode` to `FlutterGemma.initialize()`, no custom storage path — so the plugin used its own default IO location (documented as the app-documents root, i.e. a `flutter_gemma` dir **sibling** of `fah_sandbox`);
- this walk lists `owned.cwd` = `<docs>/fah_sandbox` — the sibling `<docs>/flutter_gemma` (and any `.litertlm` there) is outside it, and `SandboxedExecutionEnv` cannot reach it (host-root paths outside the sandbox get remapped inside it).

Desktop is fine (cwd = the app-support container itself, exactly what the new tests model). But if the plugin's mobile layout is indeed `<docs>/flutter_gemma`, this cleanup deletes nothing on Android/iOS — the artifacts gh-2004 promised to drop survive forever (a few-GB regression on phones).

Please confirm against the flutter_gemma source (pub package, gone from this tree): if it stores under `<docs>/flutter_gemma`, resolve the walk root on mobile to the app-documents dir (e.g. unwrap `SandboxedExecutionEnv` to its delegate in `AppOwnedEnv`, or expose the documents root the way `AppStorageCwd` does) — the exact-name + `depth == 0` anchor from this review keeps that walk just as safe. If it stores inside the sandbox, a one-line doc note here ("mobile plugin storage lives inside the fah_sandbox") closes the question for the next reader.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the consolidation reworded the non-goal stack's no-tools note — "(via transformers.js)" → "(transformers.js)"**

The `{{engine}}` dedup is a clean win (one source, `requiredToken` enforced by `gen_prompts.dart`, both codecs + tests aligned). Note that it also normalizes the transformers.js wording: the old note said "runs on-device **(via transformers.js)**", the shared note renders "runs on-device **(transformers.js)**". WebLLM text is byte-identical; transformers.js (a stack the ticket explicitly keeps out of scope) gets a one-word model-visible change.

Almost certainly fine, but since it rides a removal PR that otherwise leaves the non-goal stacks untouched: confirm the wording change is intentional (and the `{{engine}}` placeholder can never leak — the `requiredToken` gate + the two `replaceAll` call sites cover it; an engine-less future caller would emit a literal `{{engine}}` to the model, so a debug assert in `gen_prompts` output consumers would be the only hard fence — not worth it today).
